reasons: Placeholder fallback values hide setup problems.

terms.meaning: A cloud service that provides a database and user sign-in.
A public key that lets the app talk to the cloud database under its security rules.
A named setting stored outside the code and read when the app runs.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Connection settings
sections.what: Reads the cloud address and public key from settings. If they are missing, it uses fake placeholder values and records that the cloud is not set up.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app still runs when no cloud is configured.
sections.watch_out: Always check the configured flag before calling the cloud, because placeholder calls will fail.

sections.name: supabase
sections.title: Shared cloud client
sections.what: Creates the one shared cloud connection that keeps the sign-in session and refreshes it automatically.
sections.why: Likely reason: one connection for the whole app.
sections.watch_out: The session is stored in the browser, so anyone using that browser can reach the signed-in account.

summary: Creates the connection to the cloud database and checks whether it has been set up.
purpose: Gives the rest of the app one shared connection for login and cloud data.
why: Likely reason: one connection object avoids repeated setup.
how: 1) Reads the cloud address and public key from settings. 2) Uses placeholder values if they are missing. 3) Sets a flag that says whether real settings exist. 4) Creates the shared client with the session kept and refreshed.
inputs: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY settings, or the fallback names.
outputs: The shared client and the isSupabaseConfigured flag.
risks: Placeholder values mean a call made without checking the flag fails in an unclear way. The public key is meant to be public, so safety relies on database rules.
debug: If cloud calls fail, first check that the two settings exist and the flag is true. Check the browser network tab for calls to the cloud address.
